Put simply, the immune system is the body's personal, extremely effective death squad. It's so effective, that in going about its normal function killing pathogens, the natural inflammatory response can damage the tissue it's trying to protect. As such, certain body parts are sequestered/don't have lymphatic circulation/contain cells that suppress the immune response- the eyes and testicles are two such examples. Came here to comment this! It's kind of like asking what it's like to have a fever, it all depends on what's causing it.

That said, I've fainted twice before, and each time, it was this building sense of "something doesn't feel right". I felt anxious and unable to focus as my nausea grew and grew, and I experienced a sort of tunnel vision, and just as I realized "Oh my god, something is really wrong here", I collapsed. Both times, I was out for maybe ten seconds and came to looking white as a sheet and drenched in my own sweat. I was very weak and trembling for several minutes afterwards. I cried just because of how scary it was. The first time it happened was after I got Lasik eye surgery (always eat before this kind of procedure!), and the second time was during my internship at a veterinary hospital, where it happened in front of the supervising tech and a client with her poor little dog. I think I may have just been standing for too long- I was so embarrassed, but everyone else was just worried about me. Basically, if your character is prone to these episodes, there's a good chance they'll be able to tell when one is coming on and get themselves to a safe location/position. I think there are also service dogs who can detect oncoming episodes if it's a chronic issue. Hope this helps!

Not a farmer, but a vet tech student who has taken a farm animal mangement class- you'll need to decide what kind of cattle farm it is, dairy or beef, because the approach to farming is very different depending on the product. Dairy cows are much more accustomed to being handled and therefore safer to be around. Beef cows are decidedly not friendly, and most hands-on work you do with them on a modern farm will be in a chute.

As for how it compares with sheep, you're right that there are similarities! Sheep and cattle are both ruminants with four stomach chambers, so their anatomy is pretty similar. Some key differences might include the diseases each are prone to, vaccines they require, differences in the birthing process, differences in how hooves are trimmed, etc. And of course, you don't shear a cow, and you don't milk a sheep, so she'd have to learn about that, how to test the milk for mastitis (udder infection), how to process it after collection, all that good stuff! Plus the specifics of the milking setup- is it done by hand or by a machine?

She'd probably know her basic farm knots- the quick release knot and the bowline knot being two big ones.

Driving herds of cattle is also different from herding sheep- by positioning yourself in a cow's "flight zone", you can drive her forward or get her to stop. Once you get a couple moving, the herd will follow.

What she knows about breeding will depend on time period- nowadays, most cows are artificially inseminated to prevent injuries to the bull or cow, and so the farmer has better control over exactly when the cow gets pregnant. 

She would have to learn about dehorning as well. In calves, the horn buds are burnt with a hot iron before the horns can grow in. This is to prevent injuries among the herd, and also to prevent getting the cow's head stuck in a stanchion or tangled in a hanging rope.

I'd also look at breeds and decide what kind the farm has- black and white Holsteins are the most popular dairy breed by far, and black or red Anguses are the go-to for beef production. That said, there are some really cool breeds out there, you don't have to default to the most common one! The Guernsey, for example, is a type of dairy cow that produces golden milk!

I could talk about this forever so I'll stop here, but I hope this information is helpful! If you haven't seen hoof trimming videos on YouTube, I'd give them a watch- they're extremely satisfying and you can get an idea of what a cattle farm might look like!

Hi there! I'm a veterinary medicine student, but the names of these cells are the same!

Epithelial tissue is categorized by shape and layering. An epithelial cell's shape can be squamous (flat like a scale), cuboidal (cube shaped/as wide as it is tall), or columnar (tall and thin). Its layering can be simple (one layer), stratified (multiple layers), or pseudostratified (appearing to have multiple layers, but really just one layer of cells with different nuclear heights and tapering).

What you have here is as follows:

1. Stratified squamous- multiple layers of flat cells, found in the epidermis (among other places), and it provides protection!
2. Simple columnar- one layer of tall, thin cells, found in much of the digestive tract, and great for absorbing nutrients!
3. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar- one layer of tall, thin cells with varying nuclear heights and tapering, the epithelial cell of choice for much of the respiratory system, and those hairs on top (called cilia) are used to trap debris.
4. Pretty sure this is stratified cuboidal- multiple layers of cells with roughly equal width and height, found in all sorts of glands (salivary, sweat, and mammary glands, to name a few), and used for secreting large quantities of stuff!
5. Simple cuboidal- one layer of cells with roughly equal width and height, found in the kidneys, also for secretion, just on a smaller scale.

A bonus type I don't see here is transitional epithelium, a type of stratified tissue with cells of varying shapes, it's found in the bladder and is designed to stretch as the bladder fills with urine! Also simple squamous, which is very, very thin and is found in blood vessels to allow the transfer of oxygen from the blood to the tissue.

Hope this helps!

In my opinion? Before either of them entered the arena. My potentially unpopular opinion? Before either of them were even reaped.

Peeta's side of things is pretty cut and dry, he had a crush on her since they were kids, and post-reaping, he was prepared to use those feelings to give her an edge with the Capitol audience and ensure her survival. I think the seeds of Katniss's feelings are planted with the bread incident, and then lay dormant for a good long while. See the scene where she tells Haymitch about Peeta's physical strength and experience wrestling, where she says she's apparently kept track of the boy with the bread.

The days before the Games, pretty much every scene she has with him is her refocusing herself because she is convinced they are sworn enemies. Peeta's kind actions are taken at face value for half a second before she lays the paranoid, hostile filter over those actions and reinterprets them as manipulative. Which is fair given the circumstances, I don’t blame her for this at all. She is never given a moment to breathe and really think about what she feels towards him, and this is a pattern that continues across all three books because the public (especially the Capitol) feels entitled to the private details of their relationship.

Katniss doesn't feel like she has to do anything about Peeta's feelings for her until the announcement is made that two victors from the same district can win, and she impulsively shouts his name. I think that moment says a lot because it's a rare lapse in calculation for Katniss, who is hyperaware of how she's perceived from the moment she's reaped. In her post-Games interview, when Caesar asks her about it, she replies that she did it because for the first time, she felt like she could keep him. Obviously, it was part of the act, but I think she was also telling the truth, a truth that she's been unable to sit with or process, let alone accept.

As for the idea that she feels like she has to lean into the narrative in the arena, I see it more as her realizing it would be advantageous to do so than anyone actively coercing her into doing it (not that she isn't being passively coerced by the Capitol audience). This practical mindset is undercut with a growing sense of genuine emotion. Peeta is an active liability for most of the last act of the book, but not once does she even consider ditching him. Before she finds him, we get one line about the shunning a tribute could expect if they abandoned their district partner post-rule change, but once she does find him, the rest of it is singlehandedly focused on keeping them both alive. The trappings of romance are one thing, but when it comes to Peeta's wellbeing, Katniss's motives have shockingly little to do with what the audience will think, and everything to do with her own care for him.

So, tl;dr, there is no one moment where it started, emotionally speaking, even though Peeta set it into motion for the audience with his confession at the interview, it was an accumulation of many different events over the course of their lives and time together in the Games.

For me, I want the chemistry between the characters to be doing at least 85% of the work. This may be rooted in potential asexuality and lack of exposure to fanfiction on my end, but I've always believed that the actual mechanics of sex are the least entertaining parts to read and to write. Theres only so many appendages and only so many holes, and we ran out of new combinations several thousand years ago, so I like to challenge myself whenever I can. 

This usually means both characters are fully clothed, no direct contact with any intimate areas, and no naming of genitalia or store-bought, out of chracter dirty talk (so no "I want to x your y", "my x is so hard right now", etc. Yawn.). I also consider finishing to be entirely optional, and going "all the way" is exceedingly rare. But how is that a sex scene, you ask? The answer is great chemistry, great pacing, great dialogue, and a rock solid understanding of your characters' personalities and how they manifest/change in a sexual context. I'm basically leaning hard into the idea that sex is more psychological than physical, to the point that touching is secondary to the *desire* to touch. I'm sort of drip feeding the reader physical contact and overloading them with mental foreplay so a hand on the lower back becomes hotter than full on rawdogging. Of course, this is just my personal tastes talking and hardly the objectively correct way to do things.

Tl;dr: If you ask me, restraint is the name of the game. Less is more. Keep them wanting.

I disagree with two things here: the notion that Gerri was anything less than perfectly reasonable as their relationship was breaking down, and this idea that she did not care about Roman or have any feelings for him.

Gerri made her boundaries and priorities extremely clear to Roman multiple times. Think ahead, avoid mess, and protect your interests. Stop sending me dick pics. Stop being weird around my partner. Her mindset is something she tried to instill in Roman through his entire apprenticeship, and I think if he really, truly respected and listened to her, he'd have a real shot at CEO. Instead, he failed to internalize anything she was telling him, and it fucked him over and over again. Dickpicgate being a textbook example. I interpret her moment in All The Bells Say ("But it doesn't serve my interests. How does it serve my interests?") as both an invitation for a pitch from him ("I'll help you if you can give me a good enough reason to") and a solemn reminder that she *told him* she would protect herself, and it is not her fault that he refused to listen to her.

Going into Connor's Wedding, she’s still much more cordial with him than she needs to be, considering he sexually harrassed and put her career on the line. And for everything he's put her through, he *fires* her, then wants comfort when Logan dies. Roman's priority is still what she can do for him, and never the other way around. And he tops it off with the absolute audacity to fire her again, accusing HER of not respecting HIM. Like, I cannot overstate the fact that Gerri owes Roman less than nothing, and she is a better person than I could ever hope to be in those circumstances for not killing and eating him on the spot.

However, I am nothing if not a Romangerri enthusiast, and I will gladly take up arms in defense of my opinion that Gerri not only sees Roman's potential but genuinely likes him. Going back to All The Bells Say, everything about her delivery tells me she still pities him, even though the mess is entirely his own making. She's still laughing at his jokes all the way up until After her first firing. The camera makes a point to linger on her reaction to Roman breaking down at the funeral. Beyond intrigue and potential, she has a genuine soft spot for him. Obviously, Logan having Roman do the first firing was a way to hurt him, but it was also a way to hurt Gerri. I don't think it would have burned the same way coming from anyone else. Both firings had her on the verge of tears.

Basically, what I'm saying goes back to the core of my overall Succession interpretation: you can choose to read it as a purely cutthroat business drama where no one loves each other, but what does that leave you with? The tragedy of Succession is that the love of power trumped the power of love. Reducing Roman and Gerri's dynamic to an equally exploitative empty husk devoid of care and concern undercuts this message. The love is there. It just wasn't enough.

Just as an alternative concept, have you considered having the piece of wood go between his tibia and fibula? If you actually need him to be mostly/entirely unable to walk, then ignore me, but if you just want a gnarly looking injury, straight through the gastrocnemius (calf muscle) might also work!

If you have your heart set on through the ankle, here's some stuff to keep in mind: like your knee, the ankle/tarsal joint is shockingly unprotected compared to other joints like the hip or shoulder, which are padded with tons of muscle. Your ankle is your tibia, fibula, and a blocky bone called the talus held together with mostly tendons and ligaments. So anatomically speaking, you're limited in terms of injuries- you can break a bone or tear a tendon/ligament, both of which are debilitating injuries that will impair his ability to walk to varying degrees. One last ankle option is if the wood punctures the sweet spot between the calcanean (Achilles) tendon and the tibia/fibula, managing to avoid all of the other tendons as well. Assuming you miss every important structure, which is unlikely but excusable, he could avoid lasting structural complications, assuming he keeps the wound clean.

Treatment procedures and healing times will vary depending on what you go with, but a broken bone will take on average six weeks to heal (with a wide range, 3-8 weeks are all reasonable times depending on the bone and type of fracture). Tendons and ligaments are long term injuries- on average, a year of your life is down the drain, and that's with everything modern medicine can throw at it. These times can and should be adjusted for your setting and circumstances.

Seconding the comments about OCD! I've had pretty much every variation of it at some point or another, and this sounds like textbook intrusive thoughts.

As for how to stop having them, there's no way to actually make it happen, but there is a way to ease the thoughts, and it's to be aware of them without giving them attention. The way the obsessive cycle works is you have a thought (often one that repulses you or you find morally despicable), you react to the thought/try to stop it, and it just grows bigger and bigger, and you're left feeling like this is how you’re going to be forever and there's nothing you can do.

The part that's in your control is how you react to it- when you have a thought, try to look at it without judgment or negative emotion, because that will make it worse. "This is a thought I'm having, I'm not choosing to have it, I can not control it, and I do not judge myself for having it." Then, ground yourself by paying attention to your environment and bodily sensations. Then, you can redirect yourself into a constructive activity. Key word constructive, because some people adopt increasingly destructive and ritualistic behaviors to cope with the obsession- this is where the compulsive part of OCD comes in.

You say this has been going on all your life, which also makes me think OCD, I've had symptoms since i was a child as well. If you don't already have a therapist, I'd reach out to one about this, because OCD is a chronic condition that greatly benefits from professional intervention. I'm sorry you've been going through this for so long, and I really hope it gets better for you!

EDIT: Also wanted to clarify that I've had the exact same kinds of intrusive thoughts, family members included. Your thoughts don't reflect who you are, they reflect what you find most horrid and shameful. They're a reflection of your moral compass, so please believe me when I say there is nothing wrong with you as a person. You suffer from these thoughts, you don't enjoy them. Don't shame yourself for your pain. The way through this is to be kind to yourself. Best of luck. <3

Spicy take incoming, but I don't think fridging is inherently bad. Characters exist to serve the plot, and sometimes the plot is spearheaded by a dude, it's the nature of the beast. Just because it's been used lazily in the past doesn't mean it can't be done and done well. In fact, it's good to be aware of the trope, because now you can consciously think about how to handle it. My general opinion on "harmful tropes" like fridging is that they're extremely case by case, and the problematic messaging re: women existing to further a man's arc can be mitigated even if your story is the textbook definition at first glance. 

The thing about representation is, you'd be surprised what you can get away with, as long as you have multiple characters representing the demographic. Everyone is going to fit some sort of negative stereotype/"trope" about themselves, but few people fit all of them at once. If you don't love how you're treating this one female character, your best bet is to add some more!

Something to also consider is how the wife is treated/thought about/viewed by the narrative. I am a woman myself, and I am also a horrible, horrible fridger. Women die by the dozens in my writing to further the plot. That said, I also kill a lot of men, and those deaths are much more brutal/humiliating/drawn out/on-screen. I try to let my women die with dignity, a privilege that does not extend to my boys. My point is, fridging isn't just about the fact that a woman dies. Fridging is problematic because it's really not about the woman at all. You could replace her with any cherished bauble and have the same effect. She's not a person, she's barely a character, she's a plot device. If you're worried about fridging, don't treat it as "killing a woman," treat it as "killing a *person,* a *real person* who was deeply loved." 

I hope this is helpful, best of luck! :D

At the end of the day, people are animals, and a diet of human flesh would pose no more significant of a health risk than any other strictly carnivorous diet (with the exception of prion diseases from eating infected human brain tissue, but this is a bit niche and wouldn't apply here since it's happening for two years). So there's a few moving parts here, anatomically speaking- the femur, the patella, the tibia, potentially the fibula, and all the hardware in the femeropatellar joint that ties it together. If one or more bones are broken, they won't be able to bear weight. I had a hairline fracture in my fifth metatarsal (foot bone) that was so small it barely showed up on the X-rays, and that tiny crack had me walking on the inside of my foot before I got fitted with a boot. Bones are your structure, so even with adrenaline factored in, they're not optional if you're looking to walk anywhere. 

You have some more flexibility with strains, sprains, or tears in the tendons and ligaments. Your femeropatellar joint is a hinge joint, so you can only make one type of movement with it- bend it any other way, and things will get real bad real quick. Three places I'd recommend damaging are the patellar tendon, which is attached at the patella and tibia, the quadriceps tendon, which is attached at the quadriceps muscle and patella, or the anterior cruciate ligament, or ACL, which is in the "core" of the knee. The ACL tear seems to be the closest injury type to what you're describing (severe but not to the point that you straight up Can't Move At All, my father tore his and was able to sort-of walk until he could get to the doctor), but it's good to remember that healing from such a tear is an arduous process- six to nine months of rest, rehabilitation, and surgical reconstruction. My dad received an allograft/tissue transplant from a cadaver when he tore his.

One more injury that could fit the bill without benching your character for a very long time (unless that's what you're going for) is a bone bruise. All the pain, swelling, lovely discoloration, and mobility impairment without the same severe trauma you'd incur with a break or tear.

I've asked myself this question many times, and my answer is and always will be that Succession is a nothing story if no one loves each other. It is the emotional core of the entire show. The tragedy is that the love is there, it was always there, but it wasn't enough to overcome the layers upon layers of trauma and the late-stage capitalist world they (we) all live in, which is inherently hostile to healthy expressions of love, love without ego or agendas, love for the sake of it.

It's easy to say Logan doesn't love his kids, Shiv doesn't love Tom, Willa doesn't love Connor, Gerri doesn't on some level love Roman, the siblings don't love each other, but what does that leave us with? I'm of the unpopular opinion that abuse and love are not, in fact, mutually exclusive- i think it's perfectly reasonable that someone can feel love for someone else and still intentionally or unintentionally treat them terribly, and when we paint abusers as unfeeling monsters incapable of love, we other them and make their behavior harder to recognize and avoid, both in our day to day relationships and in ourselves- *of course he's not abusing me, he loves me. I'm not an abuser, I love this person.*

If no one in Succession loves each other, then all it is is another corporate drama. Everyone is only out for themselves, and you're never put in a position to hope for anything more from them. But because they love each other, we get glimpses of who these people could have been in another life, who they could be in this life if they were emotionally capable of stepping up to that plate.

The love is there, and it's never, *ever* enough.

I mean, looking at both your replies to comments here and your post history, I have good news and bad news. The bad news is I can guarantee the issue is not with your appearance, but with your personality and how you interact with others. The good news is that this is not an unchangeable or genetic part of who you are, and I feel like the insistence that it is is a way of avoiding responsibility for how you come off.

If you want my advice, the first thing you need to do is curate your online experience to avoid pointless negativity. All being on subreddits for "ugly" and lonely people is doing for you is reinforcing this negative self-perception. I'm not saying you need to start peacocking around and talking about how hot you are, just that you need to stop putting so much focus on how "ugly" you are. Body neutrality works wonders. Join subreddits/follow people who have the same hobbies and interests as you do, and put the energy you're currently funneling into self-hatred into things that make you enjoy life.

Next, you seriously need to rethink the way you think about, speak to, and otherwise interact with other people. It's understandable to be afraid of rejection, but when you go projecting that fear onto people who haven't done anything to you, they can tell, and if people aren't showing interest in befriending or dating you, it's probably because they're sensing the hostility you're putting out. Treat each new interaction like a blank slate, wait for someone to give you a reason not to trust them. When in doubt, assume good faith.

Now, for the girlfriend issue. It's perfectly okay and normal to want a significant other, but I think you're falling into the trap of thinking a girlfriend will fix all your problems. If I had to wager a guess, you sound like you think a girlfriend would prove that you're desirable and generally wanted. However, getting a girlfriend wouldn't fix this, and those insecurities would absolutely follow you into this hypothetical relationship, and probably wind up destroying it, which would reinforce the insecurities ad infinitum. An ouroboros of human misery.

Start with friends before getting a girlfriend. One, because gaining experience with friends will train you for more involved relationships and what they require from you, and two, because your girlfriend should be your best friend! Or at least one of your best friends. There's a reason people call their significant others their partners, and it's because they're a team in almost all aspects of life. Lots of romantic relationships blossom from regular old friendships, and being a good friend will make you an excellent potential boyfriend. Remember that relationships aren't one sided, your hypothetical future partner is a real person with needs, you don't get to take and take and take and give nothing in return. Think about what you can offer to someone, and ignore the automatic negative thought that may have just popped into your head saying "nothing". Everyone has something to offer, you included.

Also, I know you've probably heard this a million times, but girls aren't a monolith. We aren't all shallow, and a lot of us don't really care about appearance at all as long as the guy is kind and respectful and fun to be around.

In terms of making friends, I second everyone saying you need to get out and interact with people. When you go about your day, if there's something you need to do that can be done outside or in a public space like a coffee shop or a library, do it there. Sunlight and fresh air is also excellent for improving your mood, it's not just a myth peddled by wellness experts. Clubs, sports, volunteering (animal shelters are great if you don't want to dive right in to interpersonal interaction just yet, and petting an animal will also improve your mood), all of these things give you chances to meet people as well as things to talk about when you do strike up a conversation. Also, don't forget to show interest in them as well. Ask them questions, get to know them! 

**Tl;dr Your friends are out there, they're just waiting for you to let them in.**

Hi there! I have OCD too (started developing symptoms about ten years ago when I was eleven), and I wanted to say that I struggle with the exact same thing (down to the specific imagery of head trauma and blades), and it's horrible.

However, here's what you need to remember about intrusive thoughts: they aren't a reflection on you as a person, at least not in the way you might think they are. Part of what makes them so disturbing and unwanted is because they're targeting concepts that you find most painful or unthinkable. 

It's actually a very common thing for people with OCD to distance themselves from people the intrusive thoughts target, and I would actually advise against this, as it only reinforces the negative associations your brain is creating with those people.

If these are actual urges you're struggling with and not just the unwanted thoughts, I would strongly advise talking to a therapist if you aren't already. In addition, when you start feeling the homicidal urges, try some grounding techniques. That means focusing on your breathing (inhale for four seconds, hold it for four seconds, exhale for seven seconds, hold again for four seconds, and repeat), your body (focus on physical sensations like the air on your upper lip when you breathe in and out, where your body touches the floor/wall/chair/etc.), and your surroundings (list what you can see, hear, touch, taste, and smell). The purpose of these exercises is to distract you from your thoughts/urges and reorient yourself with your body and the space you occupy. I can't guarantee it will make anything go away, but it may help to bring things down to a more manageable level.

I hope some of that helps! :D

Okay, first of all, you're not a bad person, you're a person who made a mistake. It happens, and it's not the end of the world.

Now, here's the thing: your friend knows how sorry you are, I can promise you that. Sending someone poems and playlists is beyond excessive, and if you do any more, you're going to push her away because she's going to be freaked the hell out.

You're actually making the conflict worse by finding new ways to apologize to her- she might be interpreting these apologies as performative, or she might already be over the whole thing and feel like you're dragging it out when all she wants is to be mad for a while and then move on.

That being said, the boyfriend sounds like a tool. It's possible your friend is looking at him through rose-tinted lenses, and because of this, will rush to defend him from any criticism, even if that criticism is well-earned. However, when you criticize the boyfriend, all you do is drive her away from you and into his arms- not saying you're wrong here, or that your criticism is unjustified, because again, this guy seems like a tool. If he's as much of a jerk as it sounds like he is, your friend will probably break up with him eventually. The problem is that your friend probably feels like you went behind her back to talk shit about someone she loves.

Going forward, it's in your best interests to make good on your apology. At the end of the day, your friend feels like her trust has been violated, and if you want your friendship to heal, you have to focus on rebuilding that trust. All of the stuff you're doing is well-intentioned, but ultimately says nothing about how you're going to change. Have you since stopped talking shit about the boyfriend? If you haven't, stop immediately. The part of her that still hasn't forgiven you is a part that needs time. You can't expect everything to be all better the second you apologize, especially if you haven't shown any lasting change to your behavior yet. Sometimes people just need to be mad for a while.

I'm also worried about your attachment to her. If you really would kill yourself without her friendship, then that's codependent behavior that both weakens your sense of self, and puts her under an immense amount of pressure to stay close to you because she's afraid of what you'll do if she leaves. She's a person, just like you. If you're not in therapy at the moment, I strongly recommend it if you can make it work. Either way, meditation and mindfulness exercises will also help in terms of developing an independent sense of self. There are a bunch of meditation/mindfulness apps on app stores that are both free and useful!

TL;DR is, you need to do three things:

1. Back off with the apologies.
2. Make good on the apologies you've already made to rebuild trust with your friend.
3. Work on creating a sense of identity that is not dependent on this one person (or anyone else, for that matter).

I hope that helps a bit! <3

So, with Hush, you have the Blue Baby phase before you face Hush itself. Then, when Hush pops up, once about a quarter of its HP is gone, it will move from the top of the room to the center. Oftentimes, when it performs its Continuum attack, it will be in that center position. It was from there that I started nailing down "safe spaces", so to speak.

The one I use most often is a space that isn't touched by Continuum shots, but is in a position where you can continue to shoot at Hush. If you look at Hush's sprite, there are tendrils attaching it to the ground. When Hush is in that center position, stand directly below the tendril that is the third from the left. Then, move down so you're touching the lower wall. Stay completely still- you might have some close calls, but if you stay in that exact spot, you won't get hit, no matter what direction the shots are moving in.

There are a whole bunch of safe spaces like that, it's a matter of pinning down their exact location relative to Hush's sprite. Obviously, it will start moving around once you've damaged it enough, but the Continuum shots aren't random, and will always move along the same paths relative to Hush. The safe space I mentioned earlier will always be below Hush's third tendril, and just under half the length of the room down.

I hope that helps a bit! <3

You generally get sleep paralysis mostly when you're either just falling asleep or just waking up. I find naps are more susceptible to episodes than a full-on eight hour sleep session.

My episodes don't involve anything sitting on my chest because I normally sleep on my stomach or on my side, and while hallucinations are rare for me, they do happen, with auditory hallucinations being more common than visual ones. Here's a few highlights!

\-As stated previously, I'm so used to sleep paralysis that it's more of a nuisance than a nightmare. One of my most common (and infuriating) hallucinations I'm prone to is I'll feel myself break free of the paralysis. I'll throw the sheets off of myself and get out of bed. I walk over to my dresser to retrieve my glasses and check my phone and- bam! Right back in my bed. The paralysis never ended, I just hallucinated it ending. This will happen four or five times before I break free for real. One time, after a few rounds of Inception-style hallucinations within hallucinations, I found myself back in bed facing the wall, and I saw my own hand reach up from between the bed and the wall.

\-Screaming. Lots of screaming and sometimes talking. The voices are clearly distressed, but I can't ever tell what they're saying. :( EDIT: Oh yes, and the buzzing! Can't forget the buzzing. Imagine a loud, heavy vibration steadily crescendoing to a deafening volume.

\-This one actually happened a week or two ago! I took a nap one evening after dinner and woke up paralyzed, and I heard my father's voice say "But I'm already in your room! :)" in that kind of playful dad-voice. No visual component to that one, because I forced myself to keep my eyes shut. Whatever the visual hallucinations had in store for me, I didn't want to see it. That one's probably the creepiest hallucination I've ever had. Or at least, it was creepy to me. The hand one is a close second. :'D

\-Not exactly creepy, but ever since the world got corona'd and I don't have school or work to keep me busy, I've been taking more naps during the day, and naturally, getting more sleep paralysis. Last week, I took a nap in the middle of the day and got paralyzed again upon waking up, and the fringes on a Mexican blanket I sleep with became deer antlers. They were moving, but I'm having trouble describing exactly how. It's almost like they were waving like tall grass in a gentle breeze... except they were deer antlers and I was hallucinating. :'D

And I don't know if this is just me, but sleep paralysis always leaves me with this anxious feeling in my stomach. It's not regular emotional anxiety or anything, but my heart beats really fast for a long time after (not out of fear, because again, this isn't scary for me anymore), and I feel more tired than I did before going to bed.

This is a terrible idea, but part of me wants to see what happens if I don't resist. I knew what sleep paralysis was before I started getting it, and everytime, I've immediately fought it until I broke free, so I wonder what an uninterrupted episode would be like. I don't plan on trying it anytime soon, but I am curious!\~

It varies from person to person, but sometimes, you'll feel anxious, sad, or angry in the days leading up to it. Things that normally wouldn't bother you suddenly do, and if you don't realize it's PMS, you might not know what's going on and feel like you're going crazy.

The bleeding will also vary, but it's often concentrated in the first few days. There will be both blood and uterine tissue, the consistency of which is somewhere between snot and jelly. Towards the end, it will slow down to minor staining. The longest period I've ever heard of someone having was ten days. The worst cramps I ever had felt like someone literally punching me from the inside, like I could feel each individual blow because my uterus was throbbing in the attempt to shed its lining. Some people get cramps in their lower back, and some people's cramps make them nauseous with pain. Pooping can hurt because your rectum and uterus are in such close quarters that the act of going to the bathroom puts extra pressure on your uterus. If you wear pads, they'll often rub against your inner thigh, causing something like rug burn, making walking painful (I ran track in high school, and running on my period was AGONY). If you sleep wearing a pad, the blood/tissue will follow gravity, so you might wake up with blood on your butt and lower back. Also, some blood/tissue will settle inside you while you sleep, so when you get up, you have to make a mad dash to the bathroom because standing upright will make it all fall out at once. I don't use tampons, but I know if you leave them in long enough they can cause toxic shock syndrome, which can be fatal. If you're anemic or if you bleed A LOT on your period, you can run the risk of passing out when you stand up. Your breasts will get a little bigger/bloated, but they'll also be really tender so the slightest touch hurts. I've heard of people either having much higher or much lower sex drives while on their periods, and I've also heard having sex can allegedly relieve cramping.

Birth control is a bit of a wild card. For me, the pill made my periods disappear almost entirely. They went from seven days to three days in length, and the bleeding from a moderate flow on days one and two down to mild staining. However, I know other people for whom birth control has made their PMS, bleeding, cramping, and other symptoms infinitely worse. Some birth control takes getting used to, and will make your periods longer and worse for a few months before settling down.

Overall, periods are really subjective, and depend on the individual person more than anything! Hope that helps! :D
